core_obligations: Reduce the additive statement to the more precise identity for the polynomials $P_p$ (proof lines 8975-8976).

Use the splitting principle to write down the Chern roots of $\mathcal{E}_1$ and $\mathcal{E}_2$ and to observe that the concatenation of the two lists gives the Chern roots of the middle term $\mathcal{E}$ (proof lines 8976-8981).
Conclude from the shape of the polynomials $P_p$, which are additive on disjoint unions of roots (proof lines 8981-8982).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to the precise polynomial identity (proof lines 8975-8976).
Chern roots by the splitting principle and their concatenation (proof lines 8976-8981).
Additivity read off from the choice of $P_p$ (proof lines 8981-8982).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states the additivity of the Chern character in a short exact sequence of finite locally free modules, in the precise form of the identities $P_p(\mathcal{E}) = P_p(\mathcal{E}_1) + P_p(\mathcal{E}_2)$ (statement lines 8957-8972). The proof is an application of the splitting principle: the Chern roots of the middle term are the concatenation of the roots of the two ends, and the polynomials were chosen to be additive on such concatenations. The passage through the splitting principle and the identification of the root lists are the substance, so the claim is H2.
